########## axis-min-max-nullable.yaml
title: 'fix(type): add missing nullable type for the axis `min` and `max` option'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  TypeScript users can return `null` or `undefined` from axis `min` and `max` callbacks at runtime, but the current type declarations incorrectly reject that documented pattern.

  ## Desired outcome

  The type surface for axis `min` and `max` should allow nullable callback results so the declarations match the supported API.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Axis configurations whose `min` or `max` callbacks return `null` or `undefined` pass type-checking without changing the existing runtime behavior.

  '
########## axislabel-formatter-index.yaml
title: 'feat(axis): axisLabel `formatter` can receive its index for working with `customValues`'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Axis label callbacks can format the label value, but authors working with `customValues` also need to know which generated tick they are formatting in order to line up external labels correctly.

  ## Desired outcome

  `axisLabel.formatter` should receive the tick index as an additional argument so formatter logic can work reliably with `customValues`.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A formatter declared as `axisLabel.formatter(value, index)` receives the expected index for each displayed custom tick and can build labels from that position information.

  '
########## axislabel-formatter-indexing.yaml
title: 'fix(axis): refactor axisLabel formatter'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  A chart author using custom axis label values needs labels to stay aligned with the same ordinal position they supplied, even when some custom values are filtered out because they fall outside the visible axis extent. Right now the formatter callback can receive the wrong index for repeated values because the label-building path looks the position back up from the filtered tick list instead of preserving the mapped position directly.


  ## Desired outcome

  When ECharts builds axis labels from `axisLabel.customValues`, the formatter should be called with the actual index of each rendered item in that filtered label sequence, including cases where the same numeric value appears more than once. Authors should be able to rely on formatter logic that branches on the index parameter without seeing duplicated values collapse onto the first matching position.


  ## Acceptance signals

  For duplicate or repeated custom label values that remain in range, each rendered label keeps its own formatter index and produces the text a user would expect from its own slot in the sequence. Existing axis label rendering behavior, formatter signatures, and label text generation outside this indexing bug remain unchanged.

  '
########## bar-zero-size-labels.yaml
title: 'fix(bar): fix wrong label position when bar width/height is 0'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Bar labels can end up on the wrong side when a bar’s width or height is zero, which is especially visible in sparse or collapsed datasets where labels matter most.

  ## Desired outcome

  Zero-size bars should still place outside labels according to the intended axis direction and inversion rules rather than falling back to a misleading default side.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Bars with zero width or height keep their labels on the correct visual side instead of jumping to an obviously wrong position.

  '
########## candlestick-series-encode-render.yaml
title: 'fix(candlestick): fix candlestick render error with `series.encode`'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Candlestick charts can render incorrectly or fail outright when data is mapped through `series.encode`, particularly in layouts that are not the simplest default case.

  ## Desired outcome

  Candlestick rendering should honor `series.encode` correctly across supported layouts so encoded dimensions still produce a valid candlestick chart.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A candlestick series driven by `series.encode` renders with the expected orientation and geometry instead of crashing or misplacing the candle bodies and whiskers.

  '
########## cartesian-small-number-rounding.yaml
title: Fix that extreme small numbers can not be displayed in Cartesian due to the inappropriate rounding precision.
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Extremely small numeric values can disappear or produce broken tick spacing on Cartesian charts because rounding precision removes information that still matters at the displayed scale.

  ## Desired outcome

  Axis extent and tick calculation should preserve enough precision for extremely small numbers across interval, time, and log handling so those data points remain visible.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Charts built from very small values still render meaningful extents and ticks instead of collapsing the axis or rounding the data away.

  '
########## chord-export-entry.yaml
title: 'fix(chord): add missing export entry for chord chart'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Developers trying to use the chord chart from the packaged library are missing the expected export entry, which makes the feature look unavailable even though the implementation exists.

  ## Desired outcome

  The published package should expose the chord chart through the expected chart entry so consumers can import and register it normally.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Using the packaged chord chart entry no longer fails because of a missing export, and the chart can be imported the same way as other supported chart types.

  '
########## darkmode-lightness-algorithm.yaml
title: 'fix(theme): adjust dark mode color lightness algorithm'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The current dark-mode token lightness adjustment does not create enough contrast between related colors, so charts can look flat and adjacent visual states are harder to read than they should be.

  ## Desired outcome

  Dark-theme color derivation should preserve a stronger lightness contrast so derived colors remain distinguishable while still feeling like part of the same palette.

  ## Acceptance signals

  In dark mode, related colors keep a clearer visual hierarchy and no longer collapse into nearly identical shades.

  '
########## datazoom-single-point-position.yaml
title: 'fix(dataZoom): fix wrong position of the dataZoom when the series has only one data point'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  When a chart has only one data point, the slider dataZoom can compute the wrong position and render in the wrong place, which makes simple charts look broken.

  ## Desired outcome

  Slider dataZoom should place itself correctly even when the controlled series contains just a single point.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A one-point chart shows the dataZoom in the expected location instead of offsetting it because of invalid geometry calculations.

  '
########## gauge-progress-auto-color.yaml
title: 'feat(gauge): `progress.color` supports `''auto''`'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Gauge authors can already let some visuals inherit the series color automatically, but progress arcs still require manual color duplication, which makes themed gauges harder to maintain.

  ## Desired outcome

  Gauge progress should accept `progress.color: ''auto''` so the progress fill can follow the series color mapping automatically.

  ## Acceptance signals

  When `progress.color` is set to `''auto''`, the gauge progress arc adopts the expected automatic color instead of requiring an explicit hard-coded fill.

  '
########## graph-nodescaleratio-type.yaml
title: 'fix(type): fix `nodeScaleRatio` option type for graph series'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The TypeScript declaration for graph `nodeScaleRatio` is narrower than the runtime behavior, so valid numeric configurations appear illegal in editors and build checks.

  ## Desired outcome

  The public type for `nodeScaleRatio` should accept the numeric values the runtime already supports rather than implying a single fixed literal.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Developers can provide ordinary numeric `nodeScaleRatio` values without TypeScript errors, and the runtime behavior remains unchanged.

  '
########## jitter-overlap-avoidance.yaml
title: 'fix(jitter): fix overlap when there is enough space to avoid'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Chart authors using scatter jitter are still seeing points overlap even when there is enough open space within the allowed jitter band, which makes dense plots look incorrect and undermines the point of enabling jitter in the first place.

  ## Desired outcome

  When overlap avoidance is enabled, the jitter placement should consistently choose a non-overlapping position whenever a valid position exists inside the permitted movement range, and it should only fall back when the available space is genuinely exhausted.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A scatter plot with nearby points no longer leaves avoidable collisions behind, and the adjusted points stay within the same jitter budget instead of jumping randomly while free space still exists.

  '
########## js-yaml-3-14-2.yaml
title: 'chore(deps-dev): bump js-yaml from 3.14.0 to 3.14.2'
category: other
requirement: '## Context

  The development toolchain depends on `js-yaml`, and the repository needs the newer 3.14.2 patch level to keep maintenance dependencies current without changing chart behavior.

  ## Desired outcome

  Update the pinned development dependency from `js-yaml` 3.14.0 to 3.14.2 while keeping all runtime chart features and public APIs unchanged.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Contributors install the refreshed dev dependency set successfully, and no user-facing ECharts behavior changes as part of the version bump.

  '
########## label-layout-margin.yaml
title: Fix/label layout margin
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Chart authors are hitting inconsistent label spacing and overlap behavior across pie charts and shared label layout code, especially around margins, stroke-aware bounds, and post-layout updates.

  ## Desired outcome

  Label layout should apply the same geometry rules everywhere so `minMargin`, `textMargin`, hidden-overlap handling, and final label bounds behave consistently after layout adjustments.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Labels keep the intended spacing, pie labels and shared axis labels no longer drift because of inconsistent margin math, and overlap prevention reflects the final rendered label geometry.

  '
########## labelline-smooth-reset.yaml
title: 'fix(label): fix labelLine `smooth` can not be reset'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Pie labels can keep a stale curved guide line after `labelLine.smooth` is turned off or reset to zero, so option updates do not faithfully reflect the current configuration.

  ## Desired outcome

  Changing `labelLine.smooth` back to `false` or `0` should fully reset the guide line to a straight path instead of preserving the previous smoothing.

  ## Acceptance signals

  After updating `labelLine.smooth`, the rendered label line immediately matches the new setting and does not retain an old smooth curve.

  '
########## license-headers-precommit.yaml
title: 'chore: add license headers and a script of pre-commit'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Contributors currently have no consistent safeguard for Apache license headers, so missing headers can slip into the repository and only get noticed late in review.

  ## Desired outcome

  Add repository tooling that checks for required license headers before commit, including a `checkheader` workflow that surfaces missing headers clearly while leaving runtime chart behavior unchanged.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Contributors get an actionable pre-commit failure when a required header is missing, and maintainers can enforce header compliance without changing user-facing chart features.

  '
########## line-areastyle-empty-dimension.yaml
title: 'fix(line): fix areaStyle render error when dimension name is empty string'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Line series with `areaStyle` can throw a render error when a dataset uses an empty string as a dimension name, even though that data shape should still be renderable.

  ## Desired outcome

  Area rendering should tolerate empty-string dimension names instead of treating them as a fatal path through the line-series logic.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A line chart with `areaStyle` and a dataset dimension named `''''` renders normally instead of failing during area generation.

  '
########## lines-loop-symbol-flip.yaml
title: 'fix(lines): fix effect symbol flip on unidirectional loop end when `roundTrip` is not enabled'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Animated symbols on one-way looping `lines` series can briefly flip direction when they cross the loop endpoint, which makes the motion look glitchy even though the route itself is correct.

  ## Desired outcome

  When `roundTrip` is not enabled, the effect symbol should preserve a consistent forward orientation across the loop boundary instead of flipping at the turnaround point.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A unidirectional looping line animation remains visually continuous, with the effect symbol keeping the expected orientation as it passes the loop end.

  '
########## lint-changed-files-pattern.yaml
title: 'fix(workflow): fix match pattern for changed files collection in the lint action'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  The lint workflow is missing some changed TypeScript files because the diff pattern does not catch files placed directly under the source root, reducing confidence in CI coverage.

  ## Desired outcome

  Update the changed-file matching so linting includes the intended TypeScript files under the source tree, while leaving product behavior untouched.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A pull request that changes a matching source-root TypeScript file now triggers the expected lint coverage instead of slipping past the workflow.

  '
########## logscale-negative-exponent-rounding.yaml
title: 'fix(logScale): Fix incorrect rounding usage, and support data with big negative exponent.'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Log-scale charts with values that use very large negative exponents can still hit incorrect rounding paths, leading to unstable tick generation and misleading axis output.

  ## Desired outcome

  Log-scale rounding should handle extremely small values consistently so charts with tiny magnitudes remain numerically correct and readable.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A log axis fed with very small values no longer mis-rounds its scale, and the resulting ticks and labels stay stable across the supported exponent range.

  '
########## marker-z-option.yaml
title: 'feat(marker): markPoint markLine markArea support z option'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Chart authors can control stacking depth for many series elements, but marker overlays still lack the same control, which makes it difficult to layer annotations correctly over complex charts.

  ## Desired outcome

  `markPoint`, `markLine`, and `markArea` should accept a `z` option so authors can place marker overlays at the intended rendering depth without relying on brittle layering hacks.

  ## Acceptance signals

  When a marker is given an explicit `z`, it renders above or below neighboring content in the same predictable way users expect from other chart elements.

  '
########## matrix-darkmode-colors.yaml
title: 'fix(matrix): fix darkMode color'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Matrix charts in dark mode still use colors that were tuned for light backgrounds, so borders and structural surfaces can become hard to distinguish and the component looks visually broken next to the rest of the dark theme.

  ## Desired outcome

  The dark theme should provide matrix-specific colors that keep the matrix body, dividers, and borders legible and visually balanced on dark backgrounds.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A matrix rendered with dark mode shows clear separation between cells and surrounding structure, without washed-out or light-theme border colors leaking through.

  '
########## matrix-dimension-length.yaml
title: 'feat(matrix): support matrix.x/y.length for conveniently creating a headless matrix without composing an array'
category: feature
requirement: '## Context

  Creating a headless matrix currently requires authors to build explicit coordinate arrays even when they only know the desired matrix dimensions, which adds unnecessary setup overhead.

  ## Desired outcome

  Matrix definitions should allow `matrix.x.length` and `matrix.y.length` so users can declare the size of a headless matrix directly without composing placeholder arrays.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A matrix configured only with dimension lengths produces the expected headless grid structure, while existing array-based matrix definitions continue to work.

  '
########## matrix-label-api.yaml
title: Fix matrix label API
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Matrix users are seeing inconsistent label behavior because matrix labels do not reliably inherit shared text defaults, and coordinate locator ranges can become invalid in edge cases.

  ## Desired outcome

  Matrix labels should inherit `option.textStyle` the same way other labels do, and matrix coordinate lookup should handle invalid locator ranges predictably, including the `coordClamp` path instead of producing unusable results.

  ## Acceptance signals

  Matrix labels pick up the expected default text styling, and matrix coordinate calculations no longer fail or return confusing ranges when some locator values are missing or out of bounds.

  '
########## matrix-label-formatter.yaml
title: 'fix(matrix): fix matrix label formatter does not work'
category: bugfix
requirement: '## Context

  Matrix users can declare label formatters, but those formatters are not actually being applied, which makes matrix labels ignore both template strings and callback-based formatting logic.

  ## Desired outcome

  Matrix labels should honor `label.formatter` consistently, including string templates and function formatters, and formatter callbacks should receive the expected matrix label context such as `name`, `value`, and `coord`.

  ## Acceptance signals

  A matrix label configured with either formatter style renders the formatted text rather than the raw value, and callback formatters receive the documented data they need.

  '
########## notice-year-2026.yaml
title: 'chore: update NOTICE year to 2026'
category: other

name: Node CI

on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, reopened, synchronize]

concurrency:
  # Note that the `teardown-pr-preview` workflow needs the same group name
  # to cancel the running `ci` workflows
  group: ${{ github.workflow }}-${{ github.event.number }}
  cancel-in-progress: true

jobs:
  lint:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [18.x]

    steps:
      - name: Fetch commit count
        env:
          PR_COMMIT_COUNT: ${{ github.event.pull_request.commits }}
        run: |
          echo "FETCH_DEPTH=$(($PR_COMMIT_COUNT + 1))" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: ${{ env.FETCH_DEPTH }}

      - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}

      - name: Cache node modules
        id: cache-dep
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        env:
          cache-name: cache-node-modules
        with:
          path: node_modules
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-lint-${{ env.cache-name }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        if: steps.cache-dep.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: npm ci

      - name: Collect changed files
        run: |
          mkdir ~/tmp/
          git diff ${{ github.event.pull_request.base.sha }} ${{ github.sha }} --diff-filter=ACM --name-only --relative '*src/**/*.ts' > ~/tmp/changed_files
          echo -e "Changed files: \n$(cat ~/tmp/changed_files)"

      - name: Lint
        run: npx eslint $(cat ~/tmp/changed_files)

      - name: Check types
        run: npm run checktype

  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    strategy:
      matrix:
        node-version: [18.x]

    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4

      - name: Use Node.js ${{ matrix.node-version }}
        uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: ${{ matrix.node-version }}

      - name: Cache node modules
        id: cache-dep
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        env:
          cache-name: cache-node-modules
        with:
          path: node_modules
          key: ${{ runner.os }}-build-${{ env.cache-name }}-${{ hashFiles('**/package-lock.json') }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        if: steps.cache-dep.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        run: npm ci

      - name: Unit Test
        run: npm run test

      - name: Build release
        run: npm run release

      - name: Test generated DTS
        run: npm run test:dts

      - name: Pack npm tarball
        if: ${{ github.repository_owner == 'apache' }}
        id: pack-tarball
        run: |
          export PR_PREVIEW_DIR='echarts-pr-preview'
          mkdir -p $PR_PREVIEW_DIR
          npm pack -pack-destination $PR_PREVIEW_DIR
          echo "PR_PREVIEW_DIR=$PR_PREVIEW_DIR" >> $GITHUB_ENV

      - name: Save PR metadata and dist files
        if: ${{ steps.pack-tarball.outcome == 'success' }}
        id: save-pr-data
        env:
          PR_NUMBER: ${{ github.event.number }}
          PR_COMMIT_SHA: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha }}
          PR_PREVIEW_DIR: ${{ env.PR_PREVIEW_DIR }}
        run: |
          cd $PR_PREVIEW_DIR
          echo $PR_NUMBER > ./pr_number
          echo $PR_COMMIT_SHA > ./pr_commit_sha
          find . -type f -regex ".*\.tgz" -exec tar xvzf {} \;
          rm -f *.tgz
          echo -e "Dist files: \n$(ls -l)"

      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v4
        if: ${{ steps.save-pr-data.outcome == 'success' }}
        with:
          name: pr_preview
          path: ${{ env.PR_PREVIEW_DIR }}
          retention-days: 1
          if-no-files-found: error
